If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to capture upward momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 2–3% in early horizon (days 1–5) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (days 25–30) to account for momentum carryover.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is positive but price is declining, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in mid-horizon (days 15–25) to counteract sentiment-price mismatch.
